elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Both sentences of 7(a) are capped: "CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR ... SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM." No unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered cap reads "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and "paid" only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 7(b): "NEITHER PARTY SHALL HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS OR SPECIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "THE FOREGOING LIMITATIONS SHALL NOT APPLY TO EITHER PARTY'S ... BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The inserted carve-out sentence lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in 7(a)-(b).
"THE FOREGOING LIMITATIONS SHALL NOT APPLY TO EITHER PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" — mutual and unconditional.
Carve-out sentence expressly includes "GROSS NEGLIGENCE" for either party.
Carve-out sentence expressly includes "WILFUL MISCONDUCT" for either party.
No reference to fraud in the rendered carve-out sentence or elsewhere in the limitation clause.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out; the only other exception is the retained "EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which is not an IP carve-out (Paragraph 9 is the independent-contractor provision).

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that Company's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes; Company's liability is instead capped at fees paid, which would on its face limit its own payment exposure.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Both the Contractor sentence and the Company sentence in 7(a) impose a maximum liability cap on the same basis.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Both caps now read "THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM", replacing the indeterminate "FEES PAID ... FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES" basis.
"THE FOREGOING LIMITATIONS SHALL NOT APPLY TO EITHER PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence carves out "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" for either party.
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" expressly listed in the mutual carve-out sentence.
"WILFUL MISCONDUCT" expressly listed in the mutual carve-out sentence.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the cap is mutual, restated on a 12-months-of-fees basis, and one inserted mutual sentence places indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap. The claimed 'deviation' status and fallback target are correct.

Preferred remains short on five elements the drafter must add if escalating: (i) the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor and 'paid or payable' basis; (ii) data protection and security breach carve-out; (iii) fraud carve-out; (iv) infringement of the other party's IP carve-out; (v) an express statement that Company's payment obligations are not 'damages' subject to the cap (currently Company's cap could be read to limit its own fee-payment exposure).

Minimality holds: only the fee-basis words and one carve-out sentence changed; deletion of 'FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES' was necessary to convert the basis to 12 months of fees, and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added.

Intent preserved: 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the Contractor-side 'performance of Services under a Statement of Work' scope survive without contradiction, and the new carve-out sentence coexists with the retained Paragraph 9 exception. Note (advisory, pre-existing and not caused by this edit): the 'PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF' cross-reference points to the independent-contractor provision and is effectively dangling as a liability exception; consider correcting or deleting it in a separate pass rather than in this fallback redline.
